iut_type: End Product (BLE+USB dual-mode keyboard, Topre Corporation)
customer_question: Why does this quote require testing BAS, DIS, and HIDS profiles in addition to HOGP, when our 2021 registration of a similar keyboard model didn't require any of these?
question_variants: Why has the required test scope for an HID keyboard expanded since our last registration?
Is this new BAS/DIS/HIDS requirement a checking-rule oversight being fixed, or an intentional new rule?
actual_issue: The customer compared the new quote (requiring HOGP, BAS, DIS, and HIDS profile testing) to their 2021 registration of a similar keyboard, which only required HOGP, and wanted to understand why the scope had expanded.
plain_english_explanation: Since the new registration system took effect on July 1, 2024 last year, SIG's consistency-check rules were revised with strengthened cross-layer inconsistency detection, resulting in a cascading ('imozuru-style') increase in required test items. While the HOGP specification itself hasn't changed, products declaring HOGP HID-Device role now must also support the minimum required items of BAS, DIS, and HIDS — a requirement that wasn't enforced (likely a gap in the older checking rules) at the time of the customer's 2021 Key Board registration.
consultant_answer: This isn't a quoting error — since the new registration system began on July 1, 2024, SIG's checking rules were revised with stronger cross-layer inconsistency detection, and HOGP HID-Device role registrations now cascade into requiring the minimum items of BAS, DIS, and HIDS as well. The HOGP spec itself is unchanged; this requirement simply wasn't enforced under the older checking rules in place when your 2021 registration was done.
decision_logic: Test scope requirements are determined by the currently active SIG checking rules at the time of registration, not by precedent from a prior registration under older rules — rule changes can expand required test scope even for functionally similar products.
final_recommendation: When a returning customer questions an expanded test scope compared to a past registration, proactively explain the July 2024 checking-rule change and its cascading effect on profile role requirements, rather than letting them assume an error or arbitrary new cost.
risk_if_done_wrong: Failing to explain the rule change could lead a customer to believe the quote is an error or unjustified increase, damaging trust and delaying their decision to proceed.
